data.name: Amarjyoti
data.gender_notes: Amarjyoti is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Amarjyoti is a Sanskrit name derived from the words ‘Amar’ meaning immortal and ‘Jyoti’ meaning light. In Hindu mythology, the name is associated with the god Amarashiva, who represents immortality and enlightenment. The name evokes the idea of eternal light and the divine energy that illuminates our lives. The name Amarjyoti carries the meaning “Immortal Light” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Amarjyoti usually hope their child will grow to embody immortal light and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: The name Amarjyoti symbolizes the inner light of the soul, which is eternal and unchanging.
data.etymology: Amarjyoti belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Immortal Light.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Amarjyoti total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

historical_references.reference: Amarjyoti was the name of the legendary king of the ancient kingdom of Kashi in northern India. He is known for his extraordinary devotion towards Lord Shiva and is believed to have ruled during the late Gupta period (5th-6th centuries CE).
historical_references.context: Legendary king of Kashi, known for his devotion towards Lord Shiva

historical_references.reference: Another reference to Amarjyoti can be found in the Hindu epic Mahabharata, where he is mentioned as the father of Bhishma Pitamaha, the grandsire of the Pandava and Kaurava princes. This reference dates back to the ancient period of Indian history, around the 4th century BCE, making it one of the earliest mentions of the name Amarjyoti in historical records.
historical_references.time_period: Ancient period of Indian history, around the 4th century BCE
historical_references.context: Father of Bhishma Pitamaha in Hindu epic Mahabharata
